text.p: Mexican President Ernesto Zedillo on Wednesday inaugurated what he called the "NAFTA highway" aimed at boosting trade between Mexico and the United States.
NAFTA is the North American Free Trade Agreement, which links Mexico, the United States and Canada in a pact that eliminates most duties and tariffs among the three countries.
Zedillo dedicated the latest 62 miles (100 km) of the highway, a stretch running through this desert community in central San Luis Potosi state.
He also announced that the government would spend another $38 million this year in an attempt to complete the job, linking Mexico City to the Texas border with a modern highway.
"Today at least half of the (state) economies of the country have in this highway a wide channel for their present efforts and for their expectations of the future," Zedillo said in the ceremony.
Even with the highway incomplete, truckers move about 160,000 tonnes of products along it each day, representing about half the cargo running between the United States and Mexico, officials said.
